strengths: Well-motivated problem formulation with clear 'optimality gap' decomposition (Eq. 7) and empirical validation (Figure 1) showing heuristic metrics misalign with true token importance
Technically sound approach: oracle importance definition is sensible, NP-hardness analysis correct, convex relaxation via PAVA + greedy algorithm is theoretically justified
Pragmatic offline profiling strategy enabling zero-overhead online execution via lookup tables, with metric-universal design working across SnapKV/KeyDiff/EA
Comprehensive experimental evaluation across 16 LongBench datasets + RULER synthetic tasks, multiple model scales (7B-32B), and consistent improvements (84% performance recovery at 80% compression)

Strong empirical validation: detailed ablations (Table 3 shows +3.53 point improvement from optimality gap), effective loss visualizations (Figures 3-4) explaining baseline failures, results at multiple compression ratios (50%, 80%)
weaknesses: Oracle importance definition (Eq. 4) has circularity: requires future decoding results unavailable at prefill time in question-agnostic setting; oracle is inherently task/query-dependent yet method claims 'task-agnostic' (more accurately 'query-agnostic with task-representative calibration')

Offline profiling generalization assumptions inadequately validated: Figure 2b uses only 6 LongBench tasks (similar document-reasoning domain); RULER results show different patterns (Table 2: 69.98% vs 29.53%), suggesting limited cross-domain generalization; no out-of-distribution testing or sensitivity analysis

Limited algorithmic novelty: isotonic regression (PAVA) + greedy allocation for diminishing returns is well-established; main contribution is problem formulation rather than new techniques; Figure 2a shows convex solution matches DP perfectly

Experimental rigor gaps: no statistical significance testing or confidence intervals in Tables 1-2; some results show within-noise variance; missing recent 2025 baselines (KVZip, CriticalKV); question-agnostic evaluation is limitation not advantage

K_max parameter in oracle definition (Eq. 4) is hyperparameter without ablation study; unknown future sequence length during prefill; no analysis of oracle degradation when actual decoding window differs from calibration K_max

strengths: Well-motivated insight: Identifies clear gap between instantaneous heuristic metrics and long-horizon oracle importance, with rigorous decomposition (Eq. 7) and empirical validation (Figure 1)

Rigorous technical approach: Formal non-convexity proof, sound convex relaxation via isotonic regression, provably optimal greedy algorithm for relaxed objective, empirical validation against DP solver (Figure 2a)

Comprehensive experimental evaluation: 3 models, 2 benchmarks (16+13 datasets), multiple metrics (SnapKV, KeyDiff, EA, KVZip, CAKE), multiple compression ratios, detailed ablations showing optimality gap matters
Strong empirical results: Consistent improvements across all settings, substantial gains on challenging benchmarks (69.98% vs 37.48% on RULER-16K), minimal latency overhead
Insightful visualizations: Figures 3-4 effectively demonstrate loss distribution improvements and reveal failure modes of baselines (PyramidKV layer spikes, AdaKV head imbalance)
Practical offline profiling approach: Achieves desirable properties shown in Figure 2b; Appendix F.2 validates transferability; enables deployment without online optimization
Honest limitations discussion: Impact statement appropriately flags domain shift risks and need for validation
weaknesses: Misleading 'task-agnostic' framing: Method requires task-specific offline profiling (4K tokens, 30 questions, full-attention oracle computation); only the inference time is task-agnostic. Appendix F.2 shows non-trivial variation between profiling corpora (47.16 vs 46.67 at σ=80%)

Simplistic oracle definition: Eq. 4 captures only maximum future attention, ignoring average/cumulative utility. K_max specification relegated to appendix despite significant impact on rankings. No validation that this oracle truly represents long-horizon utility beyond empirical performance

Unquantified profiling cost: Computing oracle importance requires expensive full-attention inference over dense grid (30 queries × ~100 compression ratios). No runtime analysis provided—practitioners cannot assess feasibility. Recomputation frequency not discussed

Limited domain shift analysis: Figure 2b shows consistency across QA/retrieval tasks, but all remain in same domain. More systematic evaluation needed for distribution shifts (e.g., financial vs. narrative text). Only two profiling corpora tested; more comprehensive analysis required

Modest improvements on naturalistic benchmarks: ~3% absolute improvement on LongBench (45.79 vs 41.89 for Mistral-SnapKV) versus much larger gains on RULER. Ablation (Table 3) shows w/o optimality gap achieves 43.95 vs 45.79—the gap benefit is ~3%, not transformative. Paper doesn't discuss when LU-KV provides largest benefits

Convex relaxation approximation gap unanalyzed: PAVA distorts original discrete problem, but no bound on approximation quality vs. original problem. Figure 2a compares against DP on *relaxed* loss, not original. Missing: gap between relaxed greedy solution and original optimal
Greedy algorithm claim incomplete: Greedy is proven optimal for relaxed problem (Eq. 10), not original (Eq. 8). No theorem or bound on approximation ratio to original problem optimum provided

Question-agnostic compression constraint: More restrictive than query-aware methods; real deployments often access queries. Limits applicability scope. Paper justifies as 'more rigorous' but this is a different problem statement

Incomplete baseline comparisons: HeadKV relegated to Appendix F.3; no comparison with other offline allocation methods or learning-based approaches. AdaKV is most recent strong baseline; others (Uniform, PyramidKV) are weaker comparators
Lack of statistical rigor: No error bars, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Results on code tasks (Table 1) show high variance. Multiple runs not reported—stability of results unclear
Missing practical guidance: No clear criteria for when practitioners should use LU-KV, for which workloads, or how to validate appropriateness for new domains

RULER vs. LongBench divergence unexplained: 69.98% vs 37.48% on RULER vs. 45.79 vs 41.89 on LongBench suggests specialization to retrieval tasks, but paper doesn't discuss this or generality implications

strengths: Clear and compelling insight: The identification of the optimality gap between instantaneous heuristic metrics and long-horizon oracle importance is well-motivated, with Figure 1 effectively demonstrating divergence across compression ratios

Sound technical approach: Non-convexity proof (Appendix A.1) is rigorous; convex-hull relaxation via PAVA is clever; Figure 2a validates greedy solution matches DP optimum; offline profiling (Figure 2b) shows consistent allocation trends

Comprehensive experimental validation: Systematic evaluation across 3 model sizes, 2 benchmarks, 3-4 metrics, with consistent improvements (LongBench Mistral: 45.79 vs 41.89 AdaKV; RULER: 69.98% vs 37.48%), strong visualizations (Figures 3-4) eliminating 'loss bursts'
Metric and task-agnostic framework: Works with SnapKV, KeyDiff, KVZip, CAKE, EA; requires no downstream task knowledge; negligible inference overhead (Figure 5)

Thorough ablation studies and supplementary analyses: Table 3 validates optimality gap importance; Tables 9-13 test compression sensitivity, transferability, and generalization; multiple profiling data sources examined

Honest treatment of limitations: Impact statement acknowledges domain shift risks; transferability analysis provided; clear identification of baseline failure modes (PyramidKV at deep layers, AdaKV memory constraints)
Well-structured presentation: Clear problem formulation, effective use of visualizations, comprehensive appendices with implementation details, accessible writing overall
weaknesses: Profiling transferability concerns: Offline profiling uses limited synthetic data (~4k-token Chinese novel + 30 questions) vs. diverse evaluation domains. While Figure 2b shows consistency on 6 tasks, generalization to drastically different contexts (e.g., legal documents, code, 128k contexts) remains unvalidated. Table 10 shows non-negligible variation between profiling sources

Modest improvements over strong baseline: AdaKV is recent and sophisticated; typical gains are 3-8% absolute (LongBench Mistral-π₁: 45.79 vs 41.89; Qwen-π₂: 48.26 vs 42.32). Larger relative gains on synthetic RULER tasks raise questions about real-world significance
Missing statistical rigor: No error bars, confidence intervals, or multiple runs reported. Single-run evaluation lacks robustness estimates. No significance testing on reported improvements

Incomplete failure analysis: Some task-metric combinations significantly underperform (e.g., EA metric on some tasks shows <50% accuracy); no systematic analysis of when/why the method fails or its degradation modes

Vague oracle importance details: Maximum decoding window K_max in Eq. 4 not clearly specified. Sensitivity to this hyperparameter unexplored. Justification for 1% minimum retention threshold (Appendix E) not provided

Incremental contribution: Budget allocation for KV caches has prior work (AdaKV dynamic, PyramidKV structural, HeadKV offline). LU-KV's core novelty is recognizing and optimizing for the optimality gap—valuable but somewhat incremental. Oracle importance inspired by existing perturbation bounds

Reproducibility gaps: Code not provided for review. Exact PAVA implementation details missing. Hyperparameter sensitivity unexplored (profiling context length, number of questions, averaging procedure in Eq. 11). Computational cost of profiling phase not reported

Technical assumptions not fully justified: Static profile via simple averaging (Eq. 11) may lose task-specific patterns—why is averaging optimal? PAVA monotonicity enforcement may be artificially constraining the solution. Static allocation per compression ratio assumes consistency that Figure 2b only partially validates
